text:
Mackenzie Blackwood arrived at this season with a William M. Jennings Trophy from 2025-26, and he has carried on as one of the reasons Colorado is hard to score on. He's 12-4-1 with a .910 save percentage, and by our numbers he has stopped 4.8 more goals than the shots he faced usually allow (goals saved above expected), 42 allowed on 46.8 expected.

The shape of it matters. He's slightly below league average on easy shots and well above on the middle and hard ones: .754 on high-danger chances against a league .685. That's where goalies separate, though 84 high-danger shots is not a big enough sample to bank. Evolving-Hockey's numbers tell the longer story: plus-24.7 goals saved above expected in 2024-25 and plus-19.1 last season on their scale.

He has been sharpest lately, plus-5.3 over his last five starts, including shutouts of Detroit and Montreal. Our talent range puts his true save rate a touch above league average, so the bar is a good goalie, not a wall.
headline: Blackwood keeps doing Jennings work in Colorado
